- If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or neutral (0.0), model often overreacts to recent spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- When sentiment is flat (0.0) and price is trending downward, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days by 1–2% to reflect downward momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.0 values, model exhibits high variance; use median of last 5–7 days as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment shifts from 0.0 to 1.0 (or vice versa), model often misjudges direction; apply a 3-day lag correction to align with sentiment transition.
